liz (People Ops): Quick micro-kit for managers: 2-line praise, 2-line redirect, 1-paragraph career convo, plus four self-review prompts and a tiny calibration cheat-sheet. Drop into 1:1s or review comments.

devin (Eng Manager): perfect timing. can you show a redirect that calls out delivery scope without sounding punitive?

liz (People Ops): yes 1: REDIRECT (concise, non-blame)
- "[Name], youve been shipping solid work, but were seeing recurring scope expansion on multi-team projects which delays outcomes. Going forward, please post a 3-item scope checklist before starting dev (core use-case, non-goal work to defer, acceptance criteria). Ill review the checklist in the kickoff and well reassess after the next delivery."

liz (People Ops): PRAISE (public one-liner)
- "Kudos to [Name] for leading [feature] launch 1 which reduced onboarding time by X% a great cross-team effort! :tada:"

liz (People Ops): CAREER CONVO (starter paragraph)
- "Im impressed with your execution on [area]. Lets explore where you want to go next: broader stakeholder influence, technical strategy, or people leadership. Pick one focus area and two measurable stretch goals (e.g., lead a cross-functional initiative, own SDK performance improvements). Well check progress monthly and adjust support as needed."

tara (Product): can you give a one-liner for public feedback when someone asks for soft feedback in-channel?

liz (People Ops): SUGGESTED REPLY
- "Thanks for asking! Ill DM some quick notes so theyre private, and post a short highlight here when its praise-worthy. If you want public suggestions, say so."

eli (Recruiter): any quick hire-related snippet for interview feedback? short ones help in panel wrap-ups.

liz (People Ops): INTERVIEW FEEDBACK TEMPLATES
- PASS (short): "Strong problem-solving, good system design examples, recommended for hire for [role level]." 
- NEEDS WORK: "Clear strengths in X, but would benefit from deeper ownership examples and cross-team communication. Recommend another loop focused on product tradeoffs."

liz (People Ops): SELF-REVIEW PROMPTS (copyable into form)
1) "Top achievement this cycle and the measurable result (what changed for customers or the team)?"
2) "One decision youre proud of and one youd change if you had a do-over. What did you learn?"
3) "Where would you like to expand your role next cycle? Offer 1-2 specific goals and how your manager can help."
4) "Feedback for your manager: one thing to start, stop, continue."

liz (People Ops): CALIBRATION CHEATSHEET (use in 15-min reviews)
- Anchor criteria (3 quick questions): 1) Impact: Did the work change an important metric or unblock others? 2) Reliability: Did they hit commitments consistently? 3) Growth: Did they learn or mentor others?
- Quick mapping: "High=Company/OKR impact + always reliable, Medium=Team-level impact + usually reliable, Low=Task-level + repeated misses"

devin (Eng Manager): this is great. any sample OKRs we can reuse for people-ops or eng teams?

liz (People Ops): SAMPLE OKRs
- "Objective: Improve first-response time for supportable API issues. KR1: Reduce median triage time from 3h to 45m. KR2: Create runbook and run 2 training sessions with CS/sdks."
- "Objective: Increase onboarding velocity for new engineers. KR1: Cut time-to-first-PR from 21 days to 10 days. KR2: Add 5 curated starter issues across core repos and assign mentors."

tara (Product): can you add a tiny timeline phrase managers can paste when they set expectation for improvement? something like "were checking in"

liz (People Ops): TIMELINE LINE (pasteable)
- "Were going to try this approach for the next 6 weeks with a 2-week check-in; well revisit progress and adjust goals then."

hr-bot: Reminder: Q2 review window opens in 10 days. Use /review-start to begin.

liz (People Ops): If you want a Google Doc with role-level versions, react with :doc: and wel prioritize a Staff pack next. Thanks!
devin (Eng Manager): thanks liz, copying these into my 1:1 notes now.
